guide.metaTitle: Install LLMnesia and search your AI history | German guide
guide.metaDescription: A German guide to installing LLMnesia in Chrome or Edge, importing your AI chat history and running your first search. App controls currently use English.
guide.title: From installation to your first search.
guide.intro: Install LLMnesia, find your first saved chat, and keep searching locally. This guide is in German. The extension, Vault web app and external payment pages currently have English interfaces.
guide.installBody: Open the listing for your browser, select its installation button and review the requested permissions. Then open LLMnesia from the browser's extensions menu. Pin it to the toolbar if you want quick access.
guide.importBody: Sign in to your own account on a supported AI platform. Open LLMnesia and use that platform's history-import option where available. Keep the required tab open while the import runs and wait for completion. Other supported conversations are indexed as you open them.
guide.importCaution: An import can only capture content your account can still access. It cannot retrieve a conversation that was deleted before LLMnesia saved it.
guide.searchBody: Press Cmd + Shift + 9 on macOS or Ctrl + Shift + 9 on Windows and Linux to open search. Enter a distinctive term from a conversation you just imported. Open a result to jump to the matching message.
guide.searchExample: Try a project name, an unusual phrase, or a place name that appears in a saved chat.
guide.shortcutNote: If the shortcut is unavailable, open search from the extension toolbar button and check your browser's extension-shortcut settings.
guide.troubleshootBody: The extension and Vault web app currently have English interfaces. The website and this guide are available in German. Your saved conversations stay in their original language.
guide.privacyBody: Free local search keeps your saved conversations and index in this browser on this device. Vault is optional and paid; enabling it adds end-to-end encrypted backup and sync. Keep your own exports if you want an additional backup.
guide.nextBody: LLMnesia indexes supported new conversations as you work. Search again when you want to find a previous answer, prompt or decision.
listing.name: LLMnesia — Search your AI chat history
listing.summary: Search saved AI chats locally. Free. German guide; app interface in English.
listing.description:
Find answers you already had. LLMnesia searches your saved AI chat history across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen and other supported tools.

Import your existing history, search indexed conversations, filter results and open the matching message. Saved copies can be read offline and exported. Conversations deleted before LLMnesia saved them cannot be recovered.

Free local search keeps your conversation content and search index in your browser on this device. No account is required. Optional paid Vault adds end-to-end encrypted backup, sync and a web app. Limited product analytics do not include conversation content or search queries.

Language: German introduction and installation guide are available at https://www.llmnesia.com/de. The extension interface, Vault and payment pages currently use English. Conversations keep their original language. Reliable German semantic search and cross-language search are not currently guaranteed.

Install in desktop Chrome or Microsoft Edge, import your supported history and start with a distinctive term from a saved conversation.

homepage.founder.p.2: I use AI constantly across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and other tools. I kept having the same frustrating experience: I knew I'd already solved something, but I couldn't remember where. Useful prompts, answers, ideas, and decisions were disappearing into chat history. I built LLMnesia to fix that for myself. Now I'm opening it up to other people who work the same way.
homepage.faq.summary.1: Is my data stored on your servers?
homepage.faq.p.2: Not when you use free local search: its index stays in your browser. Vault is a separate, optional paid service. If you choose it, LLMnesia stores an end-to-end encrypted backup that we cannot read, so your supported devices can sync.
homepage.faq.summary.2: How does local indexing actually work?
homepage.faq.p.3: When you visit a supported AI platform, LLMnesia indexes conversation content locally in your browser storage so it is searchable later. It runs automatically in the background.
homepage.faq.summary.3: Will it index my older chat history too?
homepage.faq.p.4: Yes. You can import your existing history from {{IMPORT_PLATFORM_LIST}} in a few clicks. For other supported platforms, LLMnesia indexes conversations automatically as you open them.
homepage.faq.summary.4: Which AI platforms are supported today?
homepage.faq.p.5: Supported now: {{PLATFORM_LIST}}. You can also index local Claude Code, Codex, and ZCode sessions into the same search.
homepage.faq.summary.5: Will it slow down my browser?
homepage.faq.p.6: LLMnesia is designed to stay lightweight. Indexing happens incrementally in the background while you work.
homepage.faq.summary.6: Can I delete my indexed data?
homepage.faq.p.7: Yes. You can clear all indexed data with one click from the extension settings.
homepage.faq.p.8: Yes. You can export and back up your conversation history in a portable format that you own.
homepage.faq.p.9: No account is required for local indexing and search.
homepage.faq.p.10: Local capture, imports, search, and the desktop MCP connection are free. Vault is an optional paid service for encrypted sync, backup, restore, and its web app beta.

vault.metaDescription: LLMnesia Vault is available now. Keep one end-to-end encrypted AI chat archive across your browsers and computers, with backup and an installable web app beta.
vault.copy003: Bring the history indexed in your work profile, personal profile, desktop and laptop into the same encrypted archive instead of leaving it split between machines.

vault.copy015: Keep connected browser profiles up to date and restore your encrypted archive after a lost machine or browser profile.
vault.copy016: How is Vault different from free LLMnesia?
vault.copy017: Free LLMnesia captures and searches AI chats locally in each browser profile. Vault is the optional paid service that syncs those archives across your browsers and computers, keeps an encrypted backup, and powers the Vault web app. You do not need Vault for local capture or search.
vault.copy018: What is the Vault web app?
vault.copy019: It is an installable subscriber beta at vault.llmnesia.com for searching and reading your synced archive on phone or desktop. You create and connect your first Vault in the browser extension, then unlock that existing Vault in the web app.
vault.copy021: Ask Vault is a feature inside the Vault web app beta. It answers questions across your synced history using your chosen AI provider and your own API key. Its answers are grounded in your conversations and link back to the sources they used.
vault.copy022: Which AI platforms does it cover?
vault.copy023: Vault syncs the history LLMnesia indexes from {{VALUE_A}}. Local Claude Code, Codex, and ZCode sessions are a separate source type, and can join the same archive when indexed. Vault does not maintain a separate platform list: when the extension adds support, that indexed history can join your encrypted archive too.
vault.copy024: Is syncing the opposite of local-first?
vault.copy025: No. Your local index and search still live on your device. Vault adds an encrypted copy that your own devices can share. Encryption happens before upload and LLMnesia never receives the key needed to read your archive.
vault.copy026: Do I need Vault to use MCP?
vault.copy027: No. MCP is a separate free feature for compatible desktop AI apps and works with the local archive on that computer. Vault provides encrypted sync, backup, restore and the Vault web app.
vault.copy029: The quickest route is LLMnesia Settings in the extension: open the Vault panel, start your subscription there, and Stripe Checkout opens with no second sign-in. Or subscribe here with the same email as your Vault account. Either way, Stripe activates sync automatically after payment.

mcp.metaDescription: Let Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex, ZCode and other desktop AI apps search the conversations LLMnesia has captured across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and more. Local setup, linked sources, no conversation uploads.
mcp.copy006: Install LLMnesia and import the older chats you want available. New conversations from supported AI platforms are captured automatically as you use them.
mcp.copy007: Your searchable archive stays on this computer.
mcp.copy010: Open LLMnesia → Full settings → Connect desktop AI. Enable automatic sync, install Node.js if prompted, then copy the complete command into PowerShell on Windows or Terminal on macOS.
mcp.copy011: Follow every step shown for your computer. Windows Claude Desktop users have one additional guided step.
mcp.copy014: Fully quit and reopen the browser and connected AI app when Settings tells you to. Then ask what you decided, where you solved a problem, or what you discussed before.
mcp.copy015: Every answer includes source links: the original chat where possible, otherwise the saved conversation in LLMnesia’s local Viewer.
mcp.copy017: “Why did we choose an invite-only beta?”
mcp.copy018: Bring back the options, trade-offs, and decision you reached without remembering which AI app or conversation contained it.

mcp.copy021: Find the latest useful thread, recover what you already worked through, and continue from the next step instead of reconstructing the whole project.
mcp.copy023: “Pull together what I learned about local-first apps.”
mcp.copy024: Combine useful context from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and other supported sessions into one sourced answer you can inspect.
mcp.copy026: “What does my preferred project brief look like?”
mcp.copy027: Recover the formats, patterns, and preferences you have already established. Suggested memories remain under your review and control.
mcp.copy028: Connected automatically for your user account when Claude Code is installed.
mcp.copy029: Connected automatically on macOS. Windows users get one additional guided Claude extension step.
mcp.copy030: Connected automatically, with existing settings preserved and backed up.
mcp.copy031: Connected through the Codex CLI, including the copy bundled with supported desktop apps.
mcp.copy032: Connected automatically — setup adds the server to ZCode’s user-level MCP configuration (~/.zcode/cli/config.json) with a backup first, and ZCode’s Settings → MCP shows the connection.
mcp.copy034: For other local MCP apps, setup prints a standard connection block you can paste into their settings.
mcp.copy035: Do I need the browser extension?
mcp.copy036: Yes. The MCP package does not collect conversations on its own — it only reads the corpus that the LLMnesia browser extension builds. Without the extension, every search comes back empty. The extension is free for Chrome and Microsoft Edge and captures ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Character.AI, Grok, DeepSeek and the rest of the supported platforms as you chat.
mcp.copy038: No. The corpus, the search index, and the MCP server all stay on your machine. The only network call the extension makes is the limited, anonymised product analytics covered in the privacy policy — and that never includes conversation content, prompts, replies, or search queries. The MCP server itself makes zero network calls.
mcp.copy039: Which clients can reach the server?
mcp.copy040: Desktop apps that can run a local MCP connection, including Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex and ZCode. Browser-only AI websites cannot directly reach a local connection on your computer.
mcp.copy041: What do I need to install?
mcp.copy042: The LLMnesia browser extension and Node.js 22.13 or newer. Settings detects whether you are on Windows or macOS, links to the right Node installer, tells you exactly how to open PowerShell or Terminal, and gives you the complete command to copy.
mcp.copy043: Is MCP the same as Vault?
mcp.copy044: No. MCP is free, local-only, and designed for desktop AI clients; it works without Vault. Vault is an optional paid feature for encrypted sync and backup across supported desktop devices. Using Vault can make MCP more useful by bringing more history into your local archive. Mobile Vault access is included with a Vault subscription at vault.llmnesia.com.

Its free MCP connection lets Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex, ZCode and other desktop AI apps search that history, answer from it, and link back to the source conversations. Everything stays on this computer.

pricing.copy028: Is the extension itself going to start costing money?
pricing.copy029: No. Capturing your chats, importing your history and searching it on your device are free, and that is not changing. Vault is an addition, not a fence put around something you already have.
pricing.copy030: Do I need Vault to use MCP?
pricing.copy031: No. MCP is a separate free feature. It lets compatible desktop AI apps use the local LLMnesia archive on that computer. Vault is only for encrypted sync, backup, restore, and mobile access across your devices.
pricing.copy032: What am I actually paying for?
pricing.copy033: Joining your browsers and machines together. The free extension already searches across every AI platform in the browser profile you are using. Vault is what makes that one archive instead of several, so the thing you worked out in your work profile, or on the work laptop, is there everywhere else. Backup and restore come with it. That is the part with a server behind it, which is the part that costs money to run.
pricing.copy034: What happens to my conversations if I cancel?
pricing.copy035: Nothing is deleted. Conversations already on each device remain there and stay searchable. Sync and restore from the encrypted Vault pause when the subscription ends, and resume if you renew.
pricing.copy037: Yes. Annual works out at {{VALUE_A}} a month against {{VALUE_B}} monthly, which includes one month free. Both plans are the same Vault with the same features, so the only reason to pay monthly is if you would rather not commit to a year.
pricing.copy038: Why is it a subscription and not a one-off?
pricing.copy039: Because the cost is ongoing. Storing your encrypted history and serving it to your other devices costs money every month that you keep it there, so charging once would only work until it did not. You can cancel from the billing portal at any time. Conversations already on each device stay searchable; Vault sync and restore pause until you renew.
pricing.copy041: The quickest route is LLMnesia Settings in the extension: open the Vault panel, start your subscription there, and Stripe Checkout opens with no second sign-in. Or subscribe here with the same email as your Vault account. Either way, Stripe activates sync automatically after payment; no manual grant is needed.
pricing.copy043: No. Everything is encrypted on your device with a key we never see, so what we store is meaningless without it. We cannot read your conversations and we cannot hand over what we do not have.
pricing.copy044: Does Vault work on my phone?
pricing.copy045: Yes. The installable Vault web app beta works on phone and desktop, where you can search and read your synced history. It is included in the subscription.
pricing.copy046: Does Ask Vault send my whole archive to an AI provider?
pricing.copy047: No. Ask Vault selects a bounded set of relevant material for the question and sends that directly from your browser to the provider you chose using your own API key. It does not send the whole archive, and the request does not pass through LLMnesia.
pricing.copy049: Half your thinking is on the other machine.

Vault joins every browser and computer you use into one archive, so you stop re-solving what you already worked out somewhere else, then lets you search and read that archive in the Vault web app beta.

about.metaTitle: About Keiran Flynn — Founder of LLMnesia
about.metaDescription: Keiran Flynn is the founder of LLMnesia, a local-first Chrome and Edge extension for searching AI chat history across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and 10+ platforms.
about.copy001: Keiran Flynn is the founder of LLMnesia, a local-first Chrome and Edge extension that indexes and searches AI conversations across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and other platforms.
about.copy006: LLMnesia is a free Chrome and Edge extension that automatically indexes AI conversations from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and 10+ other platforms locally in your browser. Local search needs no cloud service or account. Optional Vault adds end-to-end encrypted sync and backup across your devices, plus an installable web app beta for search and reading.
about.copy008: LLMnesia is a local-first browser extension built for people who work across multiple AI platforms daily. It runs in the background, indexing your conversations as you browse supported AI tools. When you need to find something — a solution you got three weeks ago, a decision you documented in a prompt, a code snippet you asked Claude to write — you search and it's there in seconds.
about.copy009: Free local search keeps its index on your device. LLMnesia uses your browser's local storage to build and maintain it, and does not send conversation content or search queries to LLMnesia servers. If you deliberately enable Vault, an encrypted copy syncs through its backend so your own devices can share it.
about.copy011: LLMnesia currently indexes conversations from {{VALUE_A}}. You can also index your local Claude Code, Codex, and ZCode sessions into the same search. Google AI Mode uses optional site access. Additional integrations are in progress.
about.copy013: When you visit a supported AI platform, LLMnesia reads the page content and stores a local index entry in your browser using the IndexedDB and chrome.storage.local APIs. The index is built incrementally — no bulk export or setup required. Search results are returned by querying that local index, so results appear immediately without any network request.
about.copy015: I use AI constantly across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and other tools. I kept having the same frustrating experience: I knew I'd already solved something, but I couldn't remember where. Useful prompts, answers, ideas, and decisions were disappearing into chat history. I built LLMnesia to fix that for myself. Now I'm opening it up to other people who work the same way.
about.copy018: The local-first architecture is not a feature — it's a constraint that shapes every technical decision. Local indexing and search do not send conversation content to LLMnesia servers. Vault is a separate opt-in service: it encrypts the archive before upload with a key LLMnesia does not hold. You can review the full distinction in the privacy policy.
about.copy019: You can clear all indexed data at any time from the extension settings. You can also export your conversation index in a portable format.
about.copy021: For bugs, questions, or feedback, use the contact form on the homepage. Messages go directly to the founder inbox.
about.copy023: Installs in seconds. No account, no setup, no data leaving your browser.
chrome.interfaceNotice: The extension, Vault web app and external payment pages currently have English interfaces. Your conversations stay in their original language. Some documentation is available only in English.
privacy.copy015: LLMnesia is a browser extension and optional local desktop MCP integration that indexes your AI conversations locally on your device. Vault is a separate, optional paid feature that adds an encrypted server backup, sync, and restore. Current Vault subscribers may also use an installable Vault web app beta to search and ask questions over an existing synced Vault. LLMnesia is built with a local-first, privacy-by-design architecture.
privacy.copy016: Your AI conversation content, conversation titles, conversation URLs, prompts, responses, search queries, extension settings, and searchable index are stored locally on your device using the Chrome Storage API (chrome.storage.local), unless you choose to opt in to Vault, an optional encrypted backup and sync feature described below. If you enable the desktop MCP integration, LLMnesia also stores a local copy of that corpus in your user profile so desktop AI apps can search it.
privacy.copy017: LLMnesia uses limited product analytics through PostHog to understand feature usage, diagnose problems, and improve the extension and the Vault web app. LLMnesia does not send AI conversation content, conversation titles, conversation URLs, prompts, responses, search queries, cookies, authentication tokens, or local index data to PostHog or any other external analytics service.
privacy.copy018: Information processed locally by the extension
privacy.copy019: LLMnesia processes the following data locally on your device to provide its core search functionality:
privacy.copy020: Conversation metadata such as titles, URLs, and timestamps from supported AI chat platforms, used to build your searchable conversation index.
privacy.copy021: Conversation content such as text from your AI conversations on supported platforms, indexed locally to enable full-text search.
privacy.copy022: Search queries entered into LLMnesia, used locally to search your on-device index.
privacy.copy023: Extension settings such as your preferences and configuration, stored locally in your browser.
privacy.copy024: This data is processed and stored on your device using the Chrome Storage API (chrome.storage.local). It is not transmitted to LLMnesia servers, PostHog, or other third parties, unless you opt in to Vault, described below.
privacy.copy025: Desktop MCP and local browser bridge
privacy.copy026: If you choose to connect LLMnesia to a supported desktop AI app, LLMnesia creates a second local conversation corpus in your operating-system user profile (by default under ~/.llmnesia/corpus). The browser extension sends conversation records to a native messaging helper running on the same computer, and the local MCP server reads and writes that corpus when the desktop AI app uses a LLMnesia tool.
privacy.copy027: The native messaging helper and MCP server do not upload conversation content, titles, URLs, prompts, responses, MCP search queries, cookies, authentication tokens, or local index data to LLMnesia, PostHog, or other third parties. The MCP server makes no analytics or advertising requests.
privacy.copy028: Desktop MCP and automatic browser sync are optional. Chrome asks you to approve native messaging access when you click Enable automatic sync in LLMnesia Settings. The local helper setup also configures the supported desktop AI apps you choose to use.
privacy.copy030: LLMnesia uses PostHog to collect limited product analytics from the browser extension and from the Vault web app beta. This helps us understand which features are used, diagnose errors, improve reliability, and make better product decisions.
privacy.copy031: Analytics events may include limited technical and usage information such as:
privacy.copy034: Supported AI platform name, such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or Perplexity
privacy.copy035: Feature interactions, such as opening the extension, starting indexing, completing indexing, or using a settings control
privacy.copy037: Aggregate counts, such as the number of conversations indexed
privacy.copy038: An anonymous extension install identifier used to understand product usage without requiring an account
privacy.copy039: Web app usage events, such as opens, sign-ins and unlocks (recorded by method only), lock and sign-out, searches (query length and result count, never the query text), Ask submissions (question length, never the question text), and transcript opens
privacy.copy040: An anonymous web app identifier: a random ID kept in the browser's localStorage on the vault.llmnesia.com origin, never an email address or account identifier
privacy.copy041: LLMnesia does not send any of the following to PostHog or any other external analytics service:
privacy.copy050: Your name, email address, or AI platform account details
privacy.copy051: PostHog analytics are used only to operate, debug, and improve LLMnesia. They are not sold, used for advertising, transferred to data brokers, or used to determine creditworthiness or for lending purposes.
privacy.copy053: All AI conversation data created or processed by LLMnesia, including your conversation index, conversation metadata, search data, and extension settings, is stored locally in your browser using the Chrome Storage API (chrome.storage.local). If you enable desktop MCP, a second local corpus is stored in your operating-system user profile so desktop AI apps can access it.
privacy.copy054: You can view, export, or delete your locally stored LLMnesia data at any time through the extension's settings.
privacy.copy056: When you visit a supported AI chat platform, LLMnesia reads conversation titles and content from the page and saves them to a local index on your device. When you search, the extension queries this local index and displays results in your browser.
privacy.copy057: AI conversation content, conversation titles, conversation URLs, prompts, responses, search queries, extension settings, and local index data are not sent to LLMnesia servers, PostHog, or other third parties, unless you opt in to Vault, described below.
privacy.copy058: Limited product analytics are sent to PostHog as described in the Product analytics section above.
privacy.copy059: If desktop MCP is enabled, searches and tool calls run against the local filesystem corpus. They do not send the query or result to LLMnesia servers or analytics services.
privacy.copy060: Vault (optional paid encrypted backup and sync)
privacy.copy061: Vault is an optional paid feature that lets you back up your conversation index and keep it in sync across your own devices. It is off unless you deliberately create a Vault. Setup requires an account, authenticated with your email address and a one-time code, plus a private passphrase and an active subscription.
privacy.copy062: If you turn Vault on, your conversation content is encrypted on your device (AES-256-GCM, with a key derived from a passphrase only you know) before it ever leaves your device. The encrypted data is then synced to LLMnesia's sync backend, hosted on Supabase, so it can be restored to your other devices.
privacy.copy063: LLMnesia's servers store encrypted conversation and memory payloads, a wrapped copy of the Vault key, record identifiers, sync versions and timestamps, deletion markers, account and sign-in information, and subscription status. Record identifiers reveal which supported AI platform a record came from. We do not have access to your passphrase or unwrapped encryption key, and cannot read or decrypt conversation text, titles, URLs, previews, saved-memory text, or search queries stored in Vault.
privacy.copy064: Because the browser extension is built to support Vault for every installation, the extension requests permission to communicate with its Supabase sync backend (https://tkgvwpaxycliwqsrufxe.supabase.co) regardless of whether you have Vault turned on. This permission is not used, and no data is sent to that backend, unless you opt in to Vault.
privacy.copy065: Every remote Vault operation—upload, download, metadata and key retrieval, sync, and restore—requires an active subscription and is enforced by the server. If the subscription lapses, conversations already stored on each device stay there and remain searchable. The encrypted server copy is not deleted, but it cannot be synced or restored until you renew.
privacy.copy066: Payments are handled by Stripe. Stripe receives the payment and billing information you enter there; LLMnesia receives the billing email address, Stripe customer/subscription identifiers, plan and status, and relevant subscription dates. LLMnesia never receives or stores your full card details.
privacy.copy067: You can sign out of Vault at any time from the extension's settings, which removes the Vault key from that device. To have your encrypted backup deleted from LLMnesia's servers entirely, or to close the Vault account, email hello@llmnesia.com from the address on the account. There is currently no self-service whole-Vault deletion button.
privacy.copy068: Vault web app beta and Ask
privacy.copy069: Current Vault subscribers may optionally use the installable Vault web app beta at vault.llmnesia.com. The web app is a reader for an existing Vault and cannot create a person's first Vault.
privacy.copy070: The web app downloads encrypted Vault records from Supabase, then decrypts and indexes them inside the browser. The readable local corpus is stored in the web app origin's IndexedDB so the device does not need to restore the complete Vault on every visit. Lock removes readable content from the page and destroys the live Vault key, but it does not erase that local corpus. Sign out offers a choice to keep the corpus for the same account's next visit or remove the web app's local corpus and caches.
privacy.copy071: The web app may store an account session, a biometric convenience-unlock record, and a provider API key on the device. These records are encrypted with device-local, non-extractable WebCrypto keys. This protects them from a copied storage dump, but it does not protect them from malicious code already running on the Vault web app origin. Signing out removes the saved provider credential and biometric record. The user can also forget a provider key from Ask settings.
privacy.copy072: Search, filtering, and transcript reading happen locally. When the user taps Ask, the web app starts a bounded Ask session using the provider and model selected in Ask settings. It sends the question and bounded relevant context directly from the browser to that provider, currently OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or OpenRouter, using the user's own API key. Ask does not send the whole Vault. The request does not pass through LLMnesia. The selected provider receives the request content and ordinary network metadata under its own privacy and data-retention terms. The completed answer links back to supporting source conversations.
privacy.copy073: The Vault web app includes the same kind of anonymous PostHog product analytics as the extension, described in the Product analytics section above. It has no crash-reporting SDK. Vercel hosts and delivers the app's static files and receives ordinary web request metadata such as IP address, user agent, and request time.
privacy.copy075: LLMnesia requests the following browser permissions, each used solely to provide core functionality:
privacy.copy076: Storage saves your conversation index and extension settings locally in your browser.
privacy.copy077: Unlimited storage allows a large local conversation index to remain available without the browser's small default extension-storage quota.
privacy.copy078: Tabs opens the correct conversation when you click a search result.
privacy.copy079: Active Tab detects which supported AI platform you are currently visiting.
privacy.copy080: Scripting injects the search overlay and indexing scripts into supported AI chat pages.
privacy.copy081: Offscreen runs local background work that needs a document context, including semantic search processing and Vault encryption/decryption.
privacy.copy082: Alarms schedules bounded background maintenance, including indexing checks, Vault sync, and subscription-status refreshes.
privacy.copy083: Native messaging, requested only when you enable automatic sync, connects the extension to LLMnesia's local helper on the same computer so desktop AI apps can use the local corpus.
privacy.copy085: LLMnesia requests host permissions for supported AI platforms:
privacy.copy089: Google AI Mode (google.com, enabled as an optional site permission)
privacy.copy098: Google AI Studio and its legacy hosts (aistudio.google.com, makersuite.google.com, studio.google.com)
privacy.copy101: These permissions are used to index supported AI conversation content locally on your device and to provide LLMnesia's search functionality. LLMnesia does not use these permissions to transmit AI conversation content, search queries, cookies, authentication tokens, or local index data to external servers.
privacy.copy102: Google AI Mode is optional. New access to google.com and www.google.com is requested only when you enable Google AI Mode in Settings and approve Chrome's permission prompt. If you approved Google access in an earlier version, Chrome may retain that grant and Settings will show the integration as enabled. Chrome grants access at the domain level because extension host permissions cannot be limited to a URL query parameter. LLMnesia limits its content script to Google Search URLs and activates conversation extraction only for full-page AI Mode results (/search with udm=50). Ordinary Google searches are not indexed. Disabling Google AI Mode removes the optional permission without deleting conversations already saved.
privacy.copy103: LLMnesia also requests a host permission for its own sync backend, hosted on Supabase (tkgvwpaxycliwqsrufxe.supabase.co), used only by Vault, the optional encrypted backup and sync feature described above.
privacy.copy104: The llmnesia.com host permission is used for the optional email-updates form and the extension's own account, pricing, support, changelog, and local-viewer handoff pages.
privacy.copy106: LLMnesia uses PostHog for limited product analytics as described above. PostHog may receive limited technical and product usage events, but it does not receive AI conversation content, conversation titles, conversation URLs, prompts, responses, search queries, cookies, authentication tokens, or local index data.
privacy.copy107: LLMnesia uses Supabase to host the Vault sync backend described above. If you opt in to Vault, your encrypted conversation data and Vault account information are stored on Supabase's infrastructure. Supabase does not have access to the encryption key needed to read the encrypted payloads.
privacy.copy108: LLMnesia uses Stripe for Vault subscriptions. Payment details are entered and handled by Stripe; LLMnesia receives the identifiers and subscription state needed to grant or pause Vault access.
privacy.copy109: Vercel hosts and delivers the optional Vault web app beta. It receives ordinary web request metadata and the web app's anonymous usage events described above, but does not receive readable Vault content, the passphrase, Vault key, search or Ask text, or provider API keys from the application.
privacy.copy110: When a user taps Ask, the selected provider, currently OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or OpenRouter, receives the current question, bounded relevant context selected for that Ask session, the user's API key, and ordinary request metadata. Ask does not send the whole Vault. The request goes directly from the browser to the provider and is governed by that provider's own terms.
privacy.copy111: The optional desktop MCP server and native messaging helper run locally and do not send conversation content or MCP queries to a third-party service.
privacy.copy112: LLMnesia does not use third-party advertising networks, data brokers, or information resellers.
privacy.copy114: We do not sell user data. We do not share user data with advertisers, data brokers, or information resellers.
privacy.copy115: Limited product analytics are processed by PostHog only to help us operate, debug, and improve LLMnesia. AI conversation content and local index data are not shared with PostHog. If you opt in to Vault, encrypted conversation payloads and the associated account and sync metadata described above are processed by Supabase solely to provide Vault.
privacy.copy116: Chrome Web Store Limited Use disclosure
privacy.copy117: LLMnesia's use of information received from Chrome APIs and supported AI chat pages is limited to providing and improving its single purpose: local indexing and search of the user's AI conversations, including the optional Vault backup and sync feature described above.
privacy.copy118: LLMnesia does not sell user data, does not use user data for advertising, does not transfer user data to data brokers or information resellers, and does not use user data to determine creditworthiness or for lending purposes.
privacy.copy119: Human access to AI conversation content is not possible through LLMnesia because AI conversation content and the searchable index are stored locally on the user's device and are not transmitted to LLMnesia servers, PostHog, or other third parties. If you opt in to Vault, your conversation content is encrypted on your device before it is stored on LLMnesia's servers, so it remains unreadable to LLMnesia there as well.
privacy.copy121: AI conversation content, conversation metadata, search queries, extension settings, and local index data are stored locally on your device. This data is protected by your device's own security measures and your browser's extension storage protections.
privacy.copy122: Unless you enable Vault, AI conversation content and local index data are not transmitted to LLMnesia's servers. Data you deliberately back up via Vault is encrypted on your device before it is sent, so its content remains unreadable to LLMnesia and Supabase.
privacy.copy124: AI conversation content, conversation metadata, search queries, extension settings, and local index data are stored locally on your device for as long as the extension is installed, unless you delete them earlier.
privacy.copy125: If you enable desktop MCP, its filesystem corpus remains on the device until you delete it. Uninstalling the local helper deliberately leaves that corpus intact so removing an integration cannot accidentally destroy your history.
privacy.copy126: If you use the Vault web app beta, its local readable corpus remains in that web origin's IndexedDB after Lock. Signing out lets you keep it for the same account's next visit or remove the corpus and PWA-owned caches. Signing out always removes the saved provider credential and biometric unlock record.
privacy.copy127: You can delete your locally stored LLMnesia data at any time by:
privacy.copy128: Using the export/delete controls within the extension's settings
privacy.copy129: Uninstalling the extension, which removes the extension's local storage
privacy.copy131: To remove the desktop MCP copy as well, run the LLMnesia MCP uninstall command and delete the corpus path it prints (normally ~/.llmnesia/corpus).
privacy.copy132: If you opt in to Vault, encrypted records are retained until you delete them while remote access is active, ask us to delete the whole Vault, or close the account. They are not deleted merely because a subscription lapses; during a lapse they cannot be synced or restored unless you renew. Deleting a conversation locally while access is paused does not remove the remote encrypted record until Vault is renewed and the deletion can sync. See the Vault section above for how to sign out or request deletion of the complete Vault.
privacy.copy133: Limited analytics data processed by PostHog may be retained for product analytics, debugging, and improvement purposes. This analytics data does not include AI conversation content, conversation titles, conversation URLs, prompts, responses, search queries, cookies, authentication tokens, or local index data.
privacy.copy135: LLMnesia is not directed to children under 13. LLMnesia does not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13.
privacy.copy136: The extension processes supported AI conversation data locally on the user's device solely to provide indexing and search. It never sends conversation content, prompts, responses, search queries, or local index data to PostHog. Vault remains optional; if deliberately enabled, it transmits only the encrypted payloads and associated account and sync metadata described above.
privacy.copy138: If we update this privacy policy, we will revise the "Last updated" date at the top of this page. Continued use of the extension or website after changes constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.
privacy.copy140: When you email hello@llmnesia.com or use our contact form, we use the details and message you provide to respond to your request. We also keep basic ticket details, including the sender name and email address, date received, subject, and status, to track it. Our email and support record providers process this information for us.
privacy.copy141: We keep support email for 12 months after the request is closed and remove resolved ticket records after 180 days. You can request deletion by emailing hello@llmnesia.com.
privacy.copy143: If you have questions about this privacy policy, please contact us at hello@llmnesia.com or via the contact form on our website.
